fabric-mirroring.title: Mirroring – Microsoft Fabric – Microsoft Learn
fabric-mirroring.notes: Mirroring in Microsoft Fabric is a low-cost, low-latency way to bring data from different systems together in one analytics platform. It continuously replicates existing data estates, including Azure databases and external sources, into OneLake, where the data is stored as Parquet-based Delta tables. The page describes three types: database mirroring copies whole databases or selected tables and keeps changes in sync, metadata mirroring syncs only catalog names, schemas and tables and exposes the data through OneLake shortcuts, and open mirroring lets applications write change data into a mirrored database through public APIs. Creating a mirrored item produces a replication process and a SQL analytics endpoint in the Fabric workspace. The mirrored data can be used from Spark, notebooks and Power BI, including Direct Lake, and shared with row-level and object-level security. A running Fabric capacity is required, and replication stops if the capacity is paused or deleted. Replication is described as near real time, not guaranteed real time, and several sources are still in preview.

financial-close.title: Financial period close workspace – Dynamics 365 Finance – Microsoft Learn
financial-close.notes: In Dynamics 365 Finance, the Financial period close workspace is the place to track period-end closing work across companies, task areas and people. Closing tasks are defined once in a template, each with a due date given relative to the period end, and a closing schedule then ties that template to a concrete period and a set of companies. From the schedule the system generates the tasks automatically, creating a separate task per company when a task spans several. Task areas group the work by responsibility, for example accounts payable, accounts receivable or general ledger, and an optional calendar limits planning to open working days. Responsible users complete tasks, can attach notes, files or links, and cannot finish a task that still depends on unfinished ones. Summary tiles and markers show overdue, blocked and remaining tasks. When the schedule is set to closed, it leaves the workspace but its history stays in the list of all period close tasks, which can be exported to Excel. Setup is done under General ledger, Period close, and each schedule allows only one template.

forecast-category.title: Capture forecast category for opportunity – Dynamics 365 Sales – Microsoft Learn
forecast-category.notes: In Dynamics 365 Sales, the forecast category on an opportunity expresses how confident the seller is that the deal will close. It also decides which column of the forecast grid includes the opportunity, so the forecast can reflect the real state of the pipeline. Pipeline is the default and marks early or stalled deals. Best case marks deals that are progressing, for example with proposals sent, but without a commitment. Committed marks deals where the customer has given a verbal or contractual commitment. Omitted removes an opportunity from all forecast totals. Won and lost are set automatically when an opportunity is closed and should not be picked by hand, because doing so can make the opportunity vanish from the forecast or distort rolled-up values. The field is changed on the opportunity form, and managers in the hierarchy see totals that include the choice. The administrator must have enabled the feature, and the described steps apply to the standard Sales Hub and Sales Professional apps.

forecast-grid.title: View and manage a forecast – Dynamics 365 Sales – Microsoft Learn
forecast-grid.notes: The forecast grid is the table view of a forecast in Dynamics 365 Sales. It shows quota attainment, pipeline status and revenue at risk, aggregated by user or territory at each level of the hierarchy and for each period. In a forecast based on the organization chart, the default columns are users, quota, committed, best case, pipeline, omitted, won and lost, where the middle columns are filled from the forecast category of each opportunity. Sellers and managers open it in Sales Hub under Performance and Forecasts, pick a forecast and a period, and can drill into the underlying opportunities or adjust values. A manual recalculate action refreshes the data, and a currency selector can be enabled by an administrator or forecast manager. The out-of-the-box forecast covers only the current month and is not stored, while a configured forecast keeps several periods and refreshes on a schedule or on demand. The grid is not supported on mobile devices, and what a user sees depends on the permissions set during configuration.

functional-location.title: Introduction to functional locations – Supply Chain Management – Microsoft Learn
functional-location.notes: In Dynamics 365 Asset Management, functional locations are elements of a technical structure, such as the functional units of a system. They are created in a hierarchy, and assets are installed on them. The structure can follow the needs of the organization, for example a functional layout for managing assets with similar behavior, a process-oriented layout based on workflows, or a spatial layout based on geographic locations or sites. From a functional location, users can set up specifications and maintenance sequences for preventive and reactive maintenance, manage installed assets, and follow active requests, work orders and faults registered against those assets. Because an asset can be installed on several functional locations during its life, costs are always assigned to the functional location where the asset was installed at that time. A stated limitation is that the structure is not flexible: once a hierarchy has been built, locations cannot be moved within it. Each functional location is managed independently within Asset Management.

fusion-development.title: Fusion development in Power Platform – Power Platform – Microsoft Learn
fusion-development.notes: Fusion development is an approach to scaling application development with low-code, in which professional developers work together with citizen developers and other makers. The page cites Gartner's description of fusion teams as distributed, multidisciplinary digital business teams that combine technology and business skills. It also allows low-code capabilities to be mixed with code-first components to build fusion applications. Three personas are named: the citizen developer or maker, who knows the business process and uses visual low-code tools; the professional developer, who works with tools such as Visual Studio or Visual Studio Code and languages such as C# or JavaScript; and the IT professional or DevOps engineer, who is responsible for application lifecycle management. The aim is to build better apps faster, with professional developers handling specialized problems while simpler recurring tasks go to makers. Pro developers and IT professionals provide a safe, managed environment where makers can work with little friction. Power Platform is described as one tool in the toolset, and the page lists no licensing prerequisites or limits.

gcc-high.title: Understand Microsoft U.S. government cloud environments for Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Copilot – Microsoft Learn
gcc-high.notes: GCC High is one of three primary Microsoft 365 government cloud environments, next to GCC and DoD, and part of the U.S. sovereign cloud for government. It is described as a more isolated environment built for elevated compliance and sovereignty requirements, sitting between GCC and DoD on the spectrum of isolation. The page points to it for organizations that handle controlled unclassified information, whose contracts require FedRAMP High, DFARS or ITAR and EAR compliance, or that need stronger separation from the commercial cloud. Typical customers are U.S. defense agencies and their contractors. Microsoft Copilot can run there entirely inside the customer's government cloud tenant, keeping prompts, responses and generated content in that cloud. Feature availability may differ from commercial environments, releases usually arrive later, and third-party integrations are more restricted in highly isolated environments. Customers must check their eligibility for government cloud offerings and remain responsible for configuring Microsoft 365 to meet their regulatory duties.

github-advanced-security.title: GitHub Advanced Security – Microsoft Azure
github-advanced-security.notes: GitHub Advanced Security is presented as the native static application security testing offering for GitHub Enterprise and Azure DevOps. For GitHub Enterprise it consists of GitHub Code Security and GitHub Secret Protection. Secret scanning with push protection looks for many types of tokens from a wide range of service providers. Code scanning analyzes code in GitHub repositories for vulnerabilities and coding errors, and Autofix, built on GitHub Copilot, suggests targeted fixes for those alerts. Supply-chain features provide automated security and version updates for dependencies, security campaigns group many alerts so fixes can be generated together, and a security overview shows the posture across repositories. A connection to Microsoft Defender for Cloud links code to runtime context. The goal is to let developers fix vulnerabilities while they work. It is sold as an add-on for GitHub Enterprise Cloud, GitHub Enterprise Server and Azure DevOps, and the page gives no pricing, supported languages or scan configuration details.

group-writeback.title: Group writeback with Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync – Microsoft Learn
group-writeback.notes: Group writeback with Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync provisions groups from Microsoft Entra ID into an on-premises Active Directory environment. One purpose is to govern AD-based applications with identity governance features, for example by placing a group in an entitlement management access package. The feature relies on a provisioning agent that runs on a Windows server and uses a service account with write permissions on the relevant group and user objects. The agent also needs LDAP access to domain controllers and global catalog queries to drop invalid membership references. Scoping can be set to selected security groups or to all security groups, the latter only with an attribute scope filter, and the provisioning job runs on a fixed schedule. Prerequisites include a Microsoft Entra ID P1 license, at least the Hybrid Identity Administrator role, and an AD schema containing the msDS-ExternalDirectoryObjectId attribute. Microsoft 365 groups, mail-enabled groups and distribution lists are not provisioned this way, and only members with an AD DS account are written back.

hadamard-gate.title: Tutorial: Implement a quantum random number generator in Q# – Azure Quantum – Microsoft Learn
hadamard-gate.notes: The Hadamard operation, written H in Q#, is a single-qubit operation used to put a qubit into superposition. When it is applied to a qubit in the zero state, the qubit ends up in an equal superposition of zero and one, so both outcomes have the same probability. The tutorial uses exactly this in a random bit generator: a qubit is allocated, H is applied, and then a measurement is made. Because of the superposition created by H, the measurement returns zero or one with equal probability, which is what makes the result usable as a random bit. Before the measurement the qubit state is a probability distribution rather than a single value. The page also shows with Bloch sphere illustrations how a qubit starting in the zero state is moved into superposition by H. It does not give the matrix form of the gate or describe its action on other input states, so it serves as a practical introduction to the gate's role rather than a formal definition.

hardware-hash.title: Register devices to Windows Autopilot – Microsoft Learn
hardware-hash.notes: A hardware hash is the hardware identity of a device that is used to register it for Windows Autopilot. For manual registration, the hash is collected and uploaded in a CSV file together with the serial number, and optionally a Windows product ID, a group tag and an assigned user. It can be captured with Microsoft Configuration Manager, with the Get-WindowsAutopilotInfo PowerShell script either to a file or directly online into Intune, from the diagnostics page during OOBE on Windows 11, or by exporting diagnostics from the work or school account settings. After a successful sync, the device appears in the Windows Autopilot devices list in Intune and is ready for deployment once an Autopilot profile is assigned. Prerequisites include an Intune subscription, Windows automatic enrollment, Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2, and a suitable Intune role. The page treats this method mainly as suited to testing and evaluation, because the device must already be booted into Windows. The CSV has strict formatting rules, and the page recommends Partner Center for most production cases.

hashicorp-packer.title: Build a Linux VM image with Packer – Azure Virtual Machines – Microsoft Learn
hashicorp-packer.notes: Packer is an open-source tool for defining and building custom machine images. On this page it is used to create custom images for Linux virtual machines in Azure, with applications and configuration already baked in; the example installs a web server on an Ubuntu base. During a build, Packer creates temporary Azure resources, starts a source VM, runs the provisioners and captures the VM as a managed image in a chosen resource group. A template defines a builder, in the example the azure-arm type with settings such as publisher, offer, SKU, location and VM size, and provisioners such as shell commands. The template can be written in JSON or HCL. Packer authenticates with a service principal that has the Contributor role on the subscription, so subscription, tenant and client details are needed, and Packer must be installed locally. Deprovisioning removes user accounts from the source VM. Azure Image Builder is named as a separate Azure service based on Packer, which can reuse existing shell provisioner scripts. The sample templates place the client secret directly in the file.

health-probe.title: Health probes – Azure Load Balancer – Microsoft Learn
health-probe.notes: A health probe in Azure Load Balancer checks whether application instances in the backend pool are reachable and responding, and load-balancer rules need one to know the state of each endpoint. The Standard SKU supports TCP, HTTP and HTTPS probes. A TCP probe succeeds when the three-way handshake to the configured port completes, while HTTP and HTTPS probes send a GET request to a given path and count only a status 200 as success. Configurable settings include protocol, port, path, interval and a threshold of consecutive successes or failures that marks an instance healthy or unhealthy. When a probe fails, the load balancer stops sending new connections to that instance, which affects inbound traffic only. Probes can also be used deliberately to steer load or to drain connections before planned maintenance. The probe source address 168.63.129.16 must be allowed in network security groups and local firewalls, the probed port must be open on the VM, and the instance must be running. Limits include no client-certificate authentication for HTTPS probes and no hostname support for HTTP probes.
